content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Distributed Testing in Apache JMeter (Master-Worker Architecture)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When conducting high-load performance testing, a single machine running JMeter often hits hardware limitations such as CPU, memory, or network bandwidth constraints. To overcome this, Apache JMeter supports a distributed testing model using a Master-Worker (formerly Master-Slave) architecture. This tutorial explains how to set up and execute distributed tests efficiently."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a distributed testing environment, the setup consists of one Master node and one or more Worker nodes:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Master Node: Controls the test, aggregates results from all workers, and generates the final reports. It does not generate load itself by default."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Worker Nodes: Receive the test plan from the master, execute the requests against the target server, and send the metrics back to the master."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Identical versions of Java installed on both Master and Worker machines."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Identical versions of Apache JMeter installed on all machines."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"All machines must be on the same local network, with firewalls configured to allow communication over the designated ports."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Configure Worker Nodes"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"On each Worker machine, you need to start the JMeter server. First, ensure you configure secure communication or disable SSL if running within a trusted private network."},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To disable SSL for simplicity in a local lab, open 'jmeter.properties' in the 'bin' directory and set the following property:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"server.rmi.ssl.disable=true"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, start the JMeter server on the worker node by executing the following command in the 'bin' directory:"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"./jmeter-server"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Configure the Master Node"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"On the Master machine, open 'jmeter.properties' and configure the remote hosts (Workers) IP addresses separated by commas."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"remote_hosts=192.168.1.101,192.168.1.102"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"Make sure 'server.rmi.ssl.disable=true' is also set on the Master node if it was disabled on the workers."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Running the Distributed Test"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can run the test via the GUI (for debugging) or via the CLI (recommended for actual load tests). To run via CLI, use the following command:"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"jmeter -n -t load_test.jmx -r -l results.jtl"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the command above, the '-r' flag instructs JMeter to run the test on all remote hosts defined in the 'remote_hosts' property of the 'jmeter.properties' file."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid using Listener elements with heavy GUIs (like View Results Tree) during distributed execution, as this can severely bottleneck the Master node."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure CSV data sets or external files used in the test plan are manually copied to the exact same relative path on all worker nodes."}]
